previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for generalized weakness and feeling unwell, with concern for a possible urinary tract infection due to his chronic indwelling Foley catheter. He had no fever, chills, or laboratory signs of infection. Blood work was unremarkable, and urine culture grew Serratia marcescens and Enterococcus, but these were considered colonizers rather than active infection. His catheter was changed, and he reported feeling much better the following morning. Weakness was likely due to mild dehydration, possibly exacerbated by high iced tea intake and heat exposure. He was discharged home with services, with adjustments to his medications including a reduced dose of citalopram and addition of docusate for constipation. Follow-up was advised with urology for routine catheter care and monitoring of a stable right renal mass.

___ y/o male with hypotonic bladder with incomplete emptying and 
chronic indwelling foley since ___ c/b frequent multidrug

generalized weakness.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Groin pain: Differential diagnosis included 
catheter-associated urinary tract infection, bacteruria, and 
trauma from Foley. Patient presenting with 1 day history of 
groin pain, which initially resolved after replacing his Foley. 
Groin pain returned though with lesser intensity. There was no 
clinical evidence of infection (no fevers, leukocytosis, flank 
pain; patient was hemodynamically stable). Patient has pyuria 
and bacteruria related to chronic foley, this is believed to 
represent bacterial colonization colonizers. Initial urinalysis 
prior to Foley change was floridly positive and culture grew 
mixed flora consistent with contamination versus colonization. 
Repeat urinalysis two days later was improved. Repeat urine 
culture is pending. Patient remained alert & oriented x 3, and 
appropriate & conversant. Patient received no antibiotics. It 
seemed most likely during this admission that presence of blood 
in urine at presentation and ongoing, intermittent groin pain 
was secondary to Foley trauma.
.
# s/p mechanical fall/generalized weakness: Per daughter, 
patient fell ~5 days prior to admission with head strike. Per 
patient and family, there were no cardiac symptoms preceding 
fall, and patient has memory of fall and time directly 
afterwards. Very likely mechanical fall. Non-contrast head CT 
was obtained, and showed no acute process. Physical therapy 
assessed patient, and recommended discharge to rehabilitation. 
Patient initially refused, and discharge was planned with 
increased home services including visiting physical therapy and 
an home attendant in addition to existing services of day care 
three days a week, and a home attendant with limited hours 7 
days a week. Patient was seen by his daughter who felt patient 
was too weak and far from baseline to go home. Patient was 
discharged to rehab.  
.
INACTIVE ISSUES:
# Coronary artery disease: s/p CABG and stenting x2. Patient was 
continued on home dose atorvastatin, metroprolol and aspirin. 
.
# Hypertension: Stable. Patient was continued on home metoprolol 
and isosorbide mononitrate. 
.
# HLN: Stable. Patient was continued on home atorvastatin.
.
# Diabetes: Stable, controlled with diet. Fasting blood glucoses 
were monitored daily.
.
# Depression: Stable. Patient was continued on home dose 
trazadone and citalopram.
.
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
-Patient's chronic indwelling Foley catheter needs to be changed 
every 4 to 6 weeks. Patient was discharged with urology 
outpatient follow-up.
-Final urine cultures still pending.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the ___ 
with bilateral groin pain. Your urinary catheter had been in 
place for more than 6 weeks, and was changed in the Emergency 
Department. After that, you had no more pain. 

A sample of your urine was taken, which showed evidence of 
bacteria in your urine. However, you had no signs or symptoms of 
an infection. We think that these bacteria in your urine are 
always there at some level, and there is no reason to treat you 
with antibiotics at this time.

We were told by your daughter that you had fallen recently and 
hit your head. She was concerned about you. We did a scan of 
your head, and found no evidence of bleeding. Because you had 
recently fallen at home, you were seen by our physical 
therapists to confirm you are safe walking at home with your 
walker. They felt that you would benefit from additional 
services, including physical therapy, and increased supervision. 
You were discharged to a ___ rehabilitation center.

your home medications exactly as prescribed.

It was a pleasure taking care of you. 
***Please remember to go and get your foley catheter changed 
every ___. Getting your foley catheter 
changed every ___ weeks is CRUCIAL to prevent further abdominal 
pain and hospitalizations.***
If you develop any concerning symptoms, please contact your 
primary care physician, or proceed to the emergency department 
in cases of emergency.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with altered mental status.

STUDY:  Portable AP upright chest radiograph.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Midline sternotomy wires and CABG graft material is unchanged.  The
patient is rotated to the left.  Chronic elevation of the left hemidiaphragm
obscures a portion of the heart, limiting assessment of its size.  The
mediastinal contours are similar to prior study and compatible with post-CABG
change.  The lungs demonstrate improved aeration of the right base, but there
is likely atelectasis in the left base.  There is no evidence of heart
failure.  There is no large pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:  Chronically elevated left hemidiaphragm with left basilar
atelectasis but no definite evidence of pneumonia.

HISTORY:  ___ male with testicular pain.

STUDY:  Scrotal ultrasound.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  The right testis measures 3.8 x 2.3 x 3.5 cm.  The left testis
measures 3.1 x 2.6 x 3.3 cm.  Both testes demonstrate normal vascularity.  In
the inferior pole of the left testis is a 2-mm echogenic region which may
represent a pearl.

The right epididymis appears normal.  The left epididymis demonstrates a large
cyst measuring 4.3 x 3.2 x 4.6 cm in its tail.

A varicocele is noted on the left.

No shadowing artifact from gas is seen, although if clinical concern for
Fournier's gangrene persists, CT may be considered.

IMPRESSION:  Left epididymal cyst and left varicocele.

INDICATION:  Patient with hypertonic bladder, indwelling Foley catheter with
multiple UTIs, leading to a fall when he hit his head.  Evaluate for
intracranial hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to head CT performed ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast axial images obtained through the brain.  Coronal and
sagittal reformations were provided.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, large mass, mass effect
or acute infarct.  Periventricular and subcortical white matter hypodensities
are again noted consistent with small vessel ischemic disease.  The ventricles
and sulci are prominent consistent with age-related parenchymal involution. 
Dense calcification is noted within the bilateral cavernous carotid arteries.
Stable 1.7 x 1.0 cm calcified mass in left posterior fossa likely represents a
calcified meningioma.  No fractures are identified.  The mastoid air cells,
middle ear cavities and paranasal sinuses are clear.  No soft tissue swelling
evident.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  to rule out acute process, to rule out pneumonia.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral radiograph of chest.  Comparisons were made with
prior chest radiographs through ___ with the most recent from
___.

IMPRESSION: 

Bilateral lung aeration has improved since ___. Right
hemidiaphragm is persistently elevated. Left lower lung atelectasis has
improved and there are no new lung opacities concerning for pneumonic
consolidation.  

Patient is status post median sternotomy with intact sternal sutures. 
Assessment of the cardiomediastinal silhouette is limited due to elevated left
hemidiaphragm and lower lung atelectasis obscuring the border.   There are no
other new relevant findings.
